sentences.text:
Author: K. Lakshman
Bench: K. Lakshman
 Honourable Sri Justice K. Lakshman
 Criminal Petition No.376 Of 2021
Order

(ORAL):
This application is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, seeking to quash the proceedings in Crime No.1 of 2021 on the file of the Station House Officer,
Narsimhulapet, Mahabubabad District, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 328,
270 and 273 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
The petitioners herein are accused Nos.1 to 3 in the above crime.

2. Heard both sides and perused the material on record.
3.

The learned counsel for the petitioners as well as the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor appearing for the State would submit that the subject matter is squarely covered by an order in Chidurala Shyamsubder v. State of Telangana1 rendered by the High Court of Judicature at Hyderabad for the States of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, and placed a copy of the said judgment for perusal.

entities.text: Chidurala Shyamsubder v. State of Telangana1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: High Court of Judicature at Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 4. In Chidurala Shyamsubder (Supra 1), a learned single Judge of the High Court following the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal2, held that the police are incompetent to take cognizance of the offences punishable under Sections 54 and 59 (1) of the Food Safety and Crl.P. No.3731 of 2018 & Batch dated 27.08.2018. 1992 Supp. (1) SCC 335 Standards Act, 2006 (for short 'FSS Act'), investigating into the offences along with other offences under the provisions of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, and filing charge sheet is a grave illegality, as the Food Safety Officer alone is competent to investigate and to file charge sheet following the Rules laid down under Sections 41 and 42 of FSS Act, whereas, in the present case, the police have registered the crime for the offences under Sections 328, 270 and 273 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

entities.text: State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Food Safety and Crl.P. No.3731 of 2018 & Batch
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Therefore, the said proceedings in Crime No.1 of 2021 on the file of the Station House Officer, Narsimhulapet, Mahabubabad District, against the petitioners herein are contrary to the principle held in Chidurala Shyamsubder (Supra 1), as such, the same are liable to be quashed.

5. In view of the above, the present Criminal Petition is allowed in terms of the order in Chidurala Shyamsubder (Supra 1) and the proceedings in Crime No.1 of 2021 on the file of the Station House Officer, Narsimhulapet, Mahabubabad District, are hereby quashed against the petitioners herein - Satyanarayana Garepally vs Assistant Subinspector Of Police on 2 February, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64892278/
1 accused Nos.1 to 3.
6.

sentences.text:
Further, since the proceedings in the aforesaid case are quashed against the petitioners herein in Crime No.1 of 2021 on the file of the Station House Officer, Narsimhulapet, Mahabubabad District,
the petitioners are at liberty to file appropriate application for return of the seized property including the seized vehicles, if any, and the learned Magistrate shall consider the same and return the seized property and vehicles on proper identification and verification of their ownership under due acknowledgment.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in the criminal petition, stand closed.

NOTE:
Registry is directed to annex a copy of the common order dated 27.08.2018 in Criminal Petition No.3731 of 2018 & batch.
